data.description:
## Summary

While shipping LLM-proxy v0.1.19, the ship wrapper was invoked with an unrecognised flag (to read help). It **ran the entire post-release sequence without performing a release**, closing 74 real release-candidate work items with the previous release's reason (`Shipped in v0.1.18`). The real release then found zero candidates and produced an empty changelog. Full incident: llm worklog **LP-0MUEALIM60037F1S**.

## Root cause

1. **No argument validation in `skill/ship/scripts/run-release.js`.** Only `--skip-checks` is wrapper-only; every other flag (including `--help`) is forwarded to `merge-dev-to-main.sh`.
2. **`merge-dev-to-main.sh` treats `-h|--help` as usage and `exit 0`** — so the child succeeds without releasing.
3. **`runReleaseImpl` does not detect the no-op release.** It skips the PR wait (no PR URL), runs a no-op `syncDevWithMain()`, then resolves `version` from `git describe --tags --abbrev=0` — the **previous** tag.
4. **`verifyReleaseMerge(version)` only checks** that the tag exists on `origin` and is an ancestor of `origin/main`. The previous tag already satisfies this, so the guard passes.
5. **`closeWorkItemsAfterRelease(version)` then closes every `stage=in_review` item with the wrong reason.**

## Overlap resolution (duplicate check, Step 4.3)

Steps 1–4 and 5's *close* trigger were fixed by the overlapping, now-completed
work item **SA-0MV0PZYMI004SUFR** ("ship: run-release.js --help runs
post-release steps and closes items against a stale tag") and its children
SA-0MV13B5F8005NT6G (fail-fast CLI), SA-0MV13B5WO008CYXA (newly-created-tag
gate) and SA-0MV13B4YT0093CKT (regression tests). Verified in the current tree:

- `parseReleaseArgs()` + `runRelease()` reject unknown flags (exit 13) and make
  `--help`/`-h` fully inert (usage, exit 0) before the Code Freeze marker or any
  gate runs.
- `snapshotReleaseTags()` / `isNewlyCreatedTag()` gate every post-release step:
  a tag that already existed before the run exits 14 without closing anything.

The remaining, still-unmet gap from the original criteria is **idempotency of
the close sweep**: `closeWorkItemsAfterRelease()` unconditionally re-issues
`wl close --reason "Shipped in v<version>"` for every candidate, so a repeated
post-release run (or an item already annotated for this version by an earlier
sweep) is re-closed and re-annotated — the 99 spurious close comments / 25
double-closed items observed in the incident. This work item now covers that
gap only.

## Desired behaviour / Acceptance Criteria (remaining gap)

- [ ] AC1: `closeWorkItemsAfterRelease(version)` skips any candidate that already carries a close marker for **this** version (`Shipped in v<version>`), with **no** `wl close` and **no** additional comment/annotation for that item; the skipped items are reported in the return value.
- [ ] AC2: The marker match is version-exact — `Shipped in v0.1.1` must not match version `0.1.18` (and vice versa); markers for other versions do not suppress a close.
- [ ] AC3: Reading the existing markers is injectable/fail-safe: an unreadable comment source logs a warning and leaves the existing close behaviour intact (a release is never blocked by the idempotency check); no test touches the live worklog.
- [ ] AC4: Regression tests cover (a) a re-run of the post-release close does not duplicate `wl close` calls or comments, (b) an item carrying another version's marker is still closed, (c) version-exact matching, (d) the unreadable-marker fail-safe path.
- [ ] AC5: Full test suite passes; `skill/ship/SKILL.md` / reference docs describe the idempotency guarantee.

## Key files

- `skill/ship/scripts/run-release.js` — `closeWorkItemsAfterRelease` (marker check), new pure helper for version-exact marker detection.
- `tests/unit/test-close-work-items-after-release.mjs` — regression tests.
- `skill/ship/SKILL.md` / `skill/ship/docs/dev/ship-skill-reference.md` — documentation.

## Already delivered by SA-0MV0PZYMI004SUFR (not re-implemented here)

- `--help`/`-h` inert; unknown flags rejected non-zero before any post-release step.
- `verifyReleaseMerge` alone is insufficient — a newly-created-tag gate now
  proves *this* run produced the release tag.
- Post-release close/notify/cleanup skipped whenever no new tag was created.
data.title: run-release.js runs post-release steps without a release: unknown flags forwarded, verifyReleaseMerge accepts the previous tag
